items.title: What Is Morph
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: What is Morph and how is it different from Electron? Build native desktop apps by compiling .mx files (JSX + TypeScript + CSS) directly into OpenGL binaries — no browser, no WebView, no runtime.

items.title: How to Install Morph on Linux
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: How to install Morph on Linux with zero runtime: the requirements (Python 3.10+, a C++23 toolchain) and every step to set up OpenGL, GLFW, and your first native build.

items.title: How to Create Your First Morph App
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: How to create your first Morph app in minutes: run morph init, write an .mx file, and run morph dev to see a native OpenGL window on screen from the terminal.

items.title: How to Configure a Morph Project
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: How to configure a Morph project: edit morph.config.json to set the entry file, window title and size, renderer, CSS, and compiler build options in one place.

items.title: How a Morph Project Is Structured
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: How a Morph project is structured: understand the src/ folder, .mx entry files, style.css, morph.config.json, and how the compiler turns them into a dist binary.

items.title: How Morph Compiles Your Code
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: How Morph works under the hood: the source to binary pipeline — tree-sitter parsing, IR building, layout, and C++ codegen that links into a single native binary.

items.title: How Morph Dev Mode Hot Reloads
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: How Morph dev mode works: morph dev keeps a live native window open, recompiles only your JS logic, and hot-swaps it over a socket without restarting the app.

items.title: How to Build a Standalone Morph Binary
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: How to build a standalone Morph app: use morph build for an optimized release binary and morph run to build-plus-run, ready to distribute with no runtime.

items.title: Morph Architecture Overview
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: How Morph's Rust compiler and C++ runtime work together: crate structure, dev/build pipelines, feature detection, version system, and distribution model.

items.title: Which HTML Elements Morph Supports
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: Which HTML-like elements Morph supports — div, span, button, input, headings, and more — and how they compile to native OpenGL nodes instead of a browser DOM.

items.title: How to Conditionally Render in Morph
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: How to show and hide parts of your Morph UI: use JSX conditional expressions and the && operator to render elements only when a condition is true.

items.title: How to Render Lists in Morph
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: How to render a collection in Morph: map over an array with {array.map(...)}, with keyed reconciliation that updates only the affected native items when data changes.

items.title: How to Handle Events in Morph
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: How to handle user events in Morph: wire onClick, onDoubleClick, onMouseDown, and keyboard events to native handlers compiled into your app.

items.title: Which CSS Properties Morph Supports
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: Which CSS properties Morph supports — layout, sizing, colors, and typography — applied at compile time to native OpenGL rendering, with all supported units explained.

items.title: How to Animate with CSS in Morph
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: How to add CSS animations in Morph: define @keyframes and run them automatically on the GPU, no hover or state change required.

items.title: How to Transition Styles in Morph
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: How to add smooth CSS transitions in Morph: animate a property change over time (like a hover) with the transition and easing properties in native rendering.

items.title: How to Transform Elements in Morph
items.author: PIYUSH

items.title: How to Use Flexbox Layout in Morph
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: How to lay out Morph UI with CSS Flexbox — the same display:flex model you know from the web, compiled to native with a two-pass layout engine.

items.title: How to Use Tailwind Classes in Morph

items.title: How Morph Compiles JavaScript to Native
items.author: PIYUSH

items.title: How State Works in Morph
items.author: PIYUSH

items.title: How Effects Work in Morph
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: How side effects work in Morph: register morphEffect to run after render and re-run when its dependencies change, tied into the component lifecycle.

items.title: How to Use Async and Fetch in Morph
items.author: PIYUSH

items.title: How JavaScript Runtime Types Work in Morph

items.title: How to Use Native C++ Types in Morph
items.author: PIYUSH

items.title: How to Call C++ from Morph JSX
items.author: PIYUSH

items.title: How to Create Custom C++ Nodes in Morph

items.title: Morph FAQ - Questions & Answers
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: Frequently asked questions about Morph: Electron vs C++, React, using npm, hot reload, and production readiness, answered in detail.

items.title: Is Morph Like Electron with Extra Steps?
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: Is Morph just Electron with extra steps? No — it's the opposite: no browser, no Chromium; your code compiles to native machine code.

items.title: Do I Need to Know C++ to Use Morph?
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: Do you need to know C++ to use Morph? No — you write .mx files; C++ is an implementation detail, optional if you want to go deeper.
keywords: do i need c++ for morph

items.title: Is Morph React? Can I Use React?
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: Is Morph React? It's React-inspired — JSX, state, effects — but there's no virtual DOM; state changes re-render native nodes directly.

items.title: Does Morph Use a Virtual DOM like React?
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: Does Morph use a virtual DOM like React? No — signals, dirty flags, and damage tracking re-render native nodes directly; there's no DOM and no diffing.

items.title: What Is Reactivity in Morph?
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: Reactivity in Morph is signals pushing into a native tree: morphState signals, automatic effects, dirty flags, and damage tracking — and why this was chosen over a virtual DOM.

items.title: Is Morph for Games or Apps?
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: Is Morph for games? It's for apps — a UI framework for native desktop applications, with an embedded OpenGL canvas for 2D and 3D content.

items.title: Can I Build Websites with Morph?
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: Can you build websites with Morph? No — it builds native desktop binaries; the web already has the best web tooling in existence.

items.title: What Happens to My JavaScript at Runtime?
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: What happens to your JavaScript at runtime in Morph? It's compiled to C++ — no interpreter, no JIT, no VM; your logic runs as native code.

items.title: Can I Use npm Packages in Morph?
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: Can you use npm packages in Morph? Not yet — but a Morph registry for UI and native C++ modules is planned, with a security-first approach.

items.title: How Does Hot Reload Work with a Compiler?
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: How does hot reload work if everything is compiled in Morph? Dev mode keeps the app running and hot-swaps the compiled logic module without restarting.

items.title: Is Morph Production-Ready?
items.author: PIYUSH
items.description: Is Morph production-ready? Not yet — the roadmap is honest about what's missing: platform support, accessibility, signing, and more.
